features.description: `python -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup repoint --plan plan.json` repoints every playlist from each extra to its keeper through crates.playlist_edit.repoint_everywhere, after recomputing the groups, writing a reverse log line per edit, and starts a scan when done.
steps: Test-first in tests/test_duplicate_cleanup.py with the N1-02 fixture: `repoint(plan, client, navidrome_db, log_path, limit=None, dry_run=False) -> dict[str, str]` keyed by extra song id with values 'repointed N playlists', 'skipped: held (<why>)', 'skipped: no longer a duplicate of <keeper>', 'skipped: keeper missing', 'refused: <playlist>: <why>', 'dry run: would repoint <names>'.

Before acting on a group, recompute: duplicate_groups over the current navidrome.db must still put extra and keeper in one group and the keeper must not be missing; otherwise skip with the reason (the plan is advice, the live DB decides).

For each unheld extra call crates.playlist_edit.repoint_everywhere(client, db, extra, keeper); every value that is not 'repointed' (refused: owned by another user, PlaylistSkew on a hidden row, PlaylistChanged, failed) is reported and the command exits 1 at the end, but the other groups are still done. Smart playlists are 'skipped: smart playlist' as repoint_everywhere reports them.

Reverse log: before each repoint_everywhere call append one JSON line per affected playlist to log_path (repoint-<UTC timestamp>.jsonl beside the plan) with {ts, playlist_id, name, extra, keeper, before, after}; the after list is the one read back. `--dry-run` writes no log and sends no updatePlaylist (assert on srv.state.requests).
After the loop, when at least one playlist was repointed and not dry_run, call client.start_scan() once (the scan between repoint and trash).

Tests: the happy path repoints pl-1 and pl-2 to s9 and the log has two lines whose before equals the fixture order; a hidden missing song in pl-1 makes that playlist 'refused' with nothing written to pl-1 and pl-2 still repointed, exit code 1; a playlist edited after the plan is still repointed correctly because repoint_everywhere reads the current entries (the plan's before/after are advice only); a keeper deleted from the fake before repoint is 'skipped: keeper missing'; running repoint twice sends no second updatePlaylist; `--limit 1` acts on one group; a group held in the plan is never touched.

features.description: `python -m scripts.duplicate_cleanup trash --plan plan.json` moves each extra to the trash with crates.trash.move_to_trash only when no playlist entry (hidden included) holds it, the keeper is on disk and listed, no scan is running and the worker lock is free; beets forgets it; everything is logged.
steps: Test-first: `trash(plan, client, navidrome_db, music_root, trash_root, lock_path, forget, log_path, limit=None, dry_run=False) -> dict[str, str]` with values 'moved to <trash path>', 'already gone', 'skipped: held (<why>)', 'skipped: no longer a duplicate of <keeper>', 'skipped: keeper missing', 'refused: still in <n> playlist entries', 'dry run: would move'.

Preconditions, each a test: raises WorkerRunning-style `CleanupRefused('stop the worker first')` when lock_path (<dirname(CRATES_DB)>/worker.lock) is held by another process (reuse sourcing.worker.hold_lock); raises CleanupRefused when client.scan_status()['scanning'] is true; an extra with any row in crates.playlist_edit.references(db, extra) is 'refused' and its file stays (a hidden missing row counts); the keeper must be a file under music_root and not missing in navidrome.db; the group is recomputed as in N1-03.

The move: crates.trash.move_to_trash(extra.path, music_root, trash_root) (its MOVES.txt line is written before the move; the test reads it back as `mv <quoted trash path> <quoted library path>`); then `forget(music_root / extra.path)` (sourcing.filer.BeetsFiler.forget in the worker; a failure is logged, not fatal); then one JSON line {ts, extra, path, keeper, trash_path} to trash-<UTC timestamp>.jsonl.
After the loop, when a file moved and not dry_run, client.start_scan() once. Exit 1 when anything was refused.

Tests (files under tmp_path/music created with real bytes): the happy path after N1-03's repoint moves s3's file to trash_root/<today>/<path>, MOVES.txt holds the reverse line, forget was called with the old absolute path, the plan's keeper file is untouched; before repoint the same call refuses with 'still in 2 playlist entries' and moves nothing; a hidden missing row in a third playlist alone blocks the move; a running scan refuses before any move; a held worker.lock refuses; `--dry-run` moves nothing and writes no log; a second run reports 'already gone' and does not call forget again; trash never overwrites (two runs on a restored file give a '(2)' name via free_path).
Commit `N1-04: duplicate_cleanup trash`.

features.description: crates/placement.py: the pure insertion rule and `place()`, which inserts a filed song into one imported playlist at its Spotify position through playlist_edit.rewrite, insert-only, with events.
steps: Test-first in tests/test_placement.py, pure rule first: `insert_index(order, entries, position)` where order is [(position, song_id or None)]: nearest earlier order row whose song is in entries -> index after that song's last occurrence; none -> before the nearest later row's song's first occurrence; none -> len(entries) (append); a neighbour Michael removed is skipped and the next one used; an order row with song None (still wanted) is skipped; returns (index, how) with how in 'after <song>', 'before <song>', 'append'.

`place(store, client, db, playlist_id, wanted_id, song_id) -> str` on the fake: returns 'placed at <index> (<how>)', 'skipped: already in playlist', 'skipped: added before (removed stays removed)' when imported_entries has it, 'skipped: not an imported playlist' unless store.is_playlist_imported, 'skipped: playlist gone' when getPlaylist 404s; refusals from playlist_edit (PlaylistSkew, PlaylistChanged, NotOwned, NotEditable) propagate as EditRefused for the caller to retry; on success mark_imported(playlist_id, [song_id]) and an event kind `placed` '<playlist name>: <artist> – <title> at <index+1> (<how>)'.
